prerequisites: Secure application of vector calculus, basics for solving differential equations, spatial reasoning.
Basic understanding of biological-chemical systems; openness for interdisciplinary thinking.
Positive completion of the StEOP (Study Entrance and Orientation Phase).

learning_outcomes.text: Understanding of the biomechanical function of the musculoskeletal, cardiovascular, and respiratory systems, as well as their anatomical and physiological foundations.
Application of dimensional analysis and scaling laws to describe biomechanical relationships.
Conveyance of the fundamental principles of point, rigid body, and continuum mechanics, as well as computer-aided investigations and their application to biological systems.
Ability to systematically analyze and solve mechanical and biomechanical problems.
Overview of interdisciplinary foundations at the interface of material sciences, chemistry, biology, and medicine.
Development of an understanding for methodological approaches and current technologies in physiological modeling and bioprinting, as well as their importance for biomedical research and application.
Explain selected chapters of biomechanics and discuss them using selected examples.
Describe biomechanical principles of the musculoskeletal and cardiovascular systems and determine the appropriate methodology for specific problems.
Explain the fundamentals of growth, biological remodeling, and healing processes in a biomechanical context.

Name applications and possibilities of computer-aided methods in biological systems. Explain the basics for obtaining, cultivating, and using biological cells in the context of bioprinting and tissue engineering.
Explain the concept and importance of preclinical and clinical studies.
Develop problems analytically, methodically, and in a solution- and design-oriented manner.
Present and evaluate biomechanical relationships as a basis for innovation competence in biomedical engineering.
Critically and constructively discuss one's own approach considering peer feedback.

syllabus_topics: Biomechanical principles of musculoskeletal and cardiovascular systems
Equations of motion, equilibrium, inertia, energy, and constitutive behavior
Imaging techniques and finite element simulation methods based on them
Collection and application of biological cells
teaching_methods: Lectures for conveying theoretical foundations (using selected examples and accompanying documents)

assessment_methods.method: Written exercise tests during the semester

assessment_rules: Assessment is based on written exercise tests conducted during the semester. Specific examination modalities are to be provided in the course information system before the semester begins.
